questions.questionText: In an investigation, the variable deliberately changed is the
questions.explanation: The independent variable is deliberately changed.

questions.questionText: Why are repeats used in an experiment?
questions.explanation: Repeats help identify anomalies and improve reliability.

questions.questionText: A ray of light entering glass from air generally
questions.explanation: Light changes direction when it enters a medium at an angle.

questions.questionText: Which energy transfer occurs in a simple electric heater?
questions.explanation: The heater converts electrical energy mainly into thermal energy.

questions.questionText: A transformer requires
questions.explanation: Transformers operate using changing magnetic fields produced by AC.

questions.questionText: Which nutrient is needed for growth and tissue repair?
questions.explanation: Proteins provide amino acids for growth and repair.

questions.questionText: Which blood component helps clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets help form clots at damaged vessels.

questions.questionText: Which force opposes motion between surfaces in contact?
questions.explanation: Friction acts against relative motion between surfaces.

questions.questionText: A convex lens can form a magnified image when the object is
questions.explanation: An object inside the focal length of a convex lens produces an upright magnified virtual image.

questions.questionText: A cyclist travels 300 m in 20 s. What is the average speed?
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells in terms of oxygen requirement, products, and energy yield. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen, breaks glucose completely to carbon dioxide and water, and releases high energy (~38 ATP) [3 marks]. Anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen during strenuous exercise, producing lactic acid and far less energy (~2 ATP) [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
(a) State three structural differences between arteries and veins. [3 marks]
(b) Explain how HIV is transmitted and give two effective ways of preventing transmission. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Arteries have thicker elastic/muscular walls, narrower lumens, and no valves (except semilunar); veins have thinner walls, wider lumens, and pocket valves [3 marks].
(b) Transmitted via unprotected sexual intercourse, infected blood transfusions/unsterilised needles, or mother-to-child [1]. Prevention: abstinence/faithful condom use, screening blood, PMTCT medication, never sharing blades/needles [2].

questions.questionText:
(a) Write the word equation for photosynthesis. [2 marks]
(b) Explain how three external factors limit the rate of photosynthesis in a greenhouse. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Carbon dioxide + Water —(light & chlorophyll)→ Glucose + Oxygen [2 marks].
(b) Low light intensity slows light-energy capture; low CO₂ concentration limits carbon fixation; low or excessive temperature slows/denatures photosynthetic enzymes [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Describe four ways a rural community can purify river water for safe drinking. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: 1. Boiling water for 1–3 minutes to kill pathogens. 2. Filtration through clean sand/charcoal/cloth to remove suspended solids. 3. Chlorination (WaterGuard/bleach) to disinfect microbes. 4. Solar disinfection (SODIS) in clear plastic bottles left in full sun [4 marks].

questions.questionText: Name the three essential mineral elements in compound NPK fertilisers and state one deficiency symptom for each in maize. [6 marks]
questions.explanation: Nitrogen (N): stunted growth and yellow lower leaves [2 marks]. Phosphorus (P): poor root growth and purplish leaves [2 marks]. Potassium (K): scorching/yellowing leaf margins and weak stems [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Outline the industrial production of oxygen and nitrogen from air by fractional distillation. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Air is filtered and cooled to remove CO₂ and water vapour [1]. Air is compressed and cooled until liquefied at -200°C [2]. Liquid air warms up in a fractionating column: nitrogen boils off first at -196°C at the top, while liquid oxygen (-183°C) is collected from the bottom [2].

questions.questionText:
An iron gate near a damp stream starts rusting.
(a) State the two conditions needed for iron to rust. [2 marks]
(b) Describe two practical methods to prevent rusting, explaining how each works. [4 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Water (moisture) and oxygen (air) [2 marks].
(b) Painting/oiling seals the iron surface away from oxygen and moisture [2]. Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which both shields the surface and sacrifices itself preferentially even if scratched [2].

questions.questionText: Describe how biogas is produced in a digester on a farm and state two advantages of using biogas over firewood. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Cow dung/organic waste mixed with water is sealed in an airtight underground tank where anaerobic bacteria digest it at warm temperature producing methane-rich biogas [3 marks]. Advantages: burns cleanly without indoor smoke pollution; reduces deforestation and yields nutrient-rich digested slurry fertiliser [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A pulley system with 4 supporting rope strands has a velocity ratio (VR) of 4. It lifts a 600 N crate using an effort of 200 N.
(a) Calculate its Mechanical Advantage. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate its percentage efficiency. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) MA = Load / Effort = 600 / 200 = 3 [2 marks].
(b) Efficiency = (MA / VR) × 100% = (3 / 4) × 100% = 75% [3 marks].

questions.questionText: State the sequence of the four strokes in a four-stroke petrol engine and explain the role of the spark plug. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: 1. Intake (piston down, petrol-air mixture drawn in). 2. Compression (both valves shut, piston compresses mixture). 3. Power (spark plug ignites compressed gas driving piston down). 4. Exhaust (exhaust valve opens, piston pushes waste gas out) [4 marks]. The spark plug supplies the high-voltage spark at the end of compression to ignite fuel [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Distinguish between mass and weight, giving the SI unit and measuring instrument for each. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body (constant everywhere), measured in kilograms (kg) with a balance [2 marks]. Weight is the gravitational pull on a body (varies with g), measured in newtons (N) with a spring balance/newtonmeter [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how a lightning conductor installed on a tall school building protects the building during a thunderstorm. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Sharp copper spikes at the top collect opposite induced charges and ionise nearby air, reducing potential difference [2 marks]. If lightning strikes, the thick copper strip safely conducts the huge electric current straight down to a buried earth plate, bypassing the building structure [2 marks].

questions.questionText: State three properties of cathode rays/electrons and explain how an electric fuse protects household appliances. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Electrons carry negative charge, have tiny mass, and deflect in electric/magnetic fields [3 marks]. A fuse contains a thin low-melting-point wire wired in series with the live wire; if current exceeds the safe rating, the wire melts and breaks the circuit before cables overheat or start a fire [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the process of eutrophication when excess chemical fertilisers wash from fields into a dam. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Leached nitrates/phosphates trigger rapid algal bloom on the surface [1]. Sunlight is blocked, submerged plants die, and decomposing bacteria multiply using up dissolved oxygen [2]. Fish and aquatic animals suffocate and die [1].

questions.questionText:
(a) Write the chemical formula of calcium carbonate and calculate its percentage by mass of calcium (Ca=40, C=12, O=16). [3 marks]
(b) State one agricultural use of limestone. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) CaCO₃; Mr = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 [1 mark]. % Ca = (40/100) × 100% = 40% [2 marks].
(b) Neutralising acidic farm soils (liming) [1 mark].
